entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned counsel for the State.

2. The applicant, who is in custody since 28.04.2022, has renewed his prayer for grant of regular bail in connection with POCSO Case No.82 of 2022, arising out of Airport P.S. Case No.24 of 2022,,
registered for the offence under Sections 376 & 376(AB) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4, 6 & 8 of the POCSO, Act, pending in the court of learned Additional Judicial Commissioner-IV,
Ranchi.
3.
The prayer for bail of the applicant was earlier rejected by this Court vide order dated 13.02.2023 passed in B.A. No.10170 of 2022.

4. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant(s) that complete set of FIR along with its enclosure have been annexed with this bail application and there is no suppression on his/her part.
5. Innocence has been claimed by the learned counsel for the applicant and undertaking has been given for participation in the trial.

It has been submitted that the victim has been examined and her Sukhair Oraon @ Langra vs The State Of Jharkhand .... .... ... on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89619911/
1 deposition suggests that offence may be due to the money transaction.

entities.text: Sukhair Oraon @ Langra vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, it has been submitted that the medical report does not corroborate the allegation against this applicant.
On the above basis, prayer for bail has been made.
6. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for bail.
7. Considering the nature of allegation and the statement of the victim girl, I am not inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail 'at this stage'.
Accordingly, his prayer for bail is hereby, rejected.
8. However, learned Trial Court is directed to expedite the trial and conclude it within six months.

(Rajesh Kumar, J.) Raja/-
